fieldFixes.contribution: In the late 1980s and early 1990s Poulsen was a notorious hacker: a 1993 federal indictment accused him of seizing control of the incoming phone lines of Los Angeles radio stations, by hacking Pacific Bell's computers, to win their contests, and of setting up his own wiretaps. After Swartz's death he launched it as Strongbox at The New Yorker in May 2013 and handed it to the Freedom of the Press Foundation, which renamed it SecureDrop, in October 2013.
fieldFixes.thread: A former intruder once charged with setting up his own wiretaps, Poulsen co-developed a system in which the recipient cannot learn who the sender is — protection that does not depend on the organisation's goodwill.
